defaultValue: Changing these settings can impact the stability of your game. Only the default configuration is tested to work.

fieldDescription: Master switch for the industries that have a switch in the Industries tab. Off is the same as turning all of them off; built industries stay. On, each industry follows its own switch. Default on. NPC placement needs a new game.

Master switch for consumable items: market stock, combat drops and the research project. Off is the same as turning off all three under Consumable Items in the Exploration & Items tab; items you own stay usable. On, each follows its own switch. Default on.
Enables salvage events as well as derelict infrastructure and industries. Off also turns off Additional Station Types. Default on. Placement needs a new game.
Artillery stations and watchtowers. Off: placed stations stop firing and can not be built. Default on. Placement needs a new game. Disabling this means you have weak bones.
Minefields around some planets. Off: mines stop hitting fleets. Default on. Placement needs a new game.
Meteor swarms. Off: no new swarms spawn. Default on.
Toggles Pets: the Animal Center, the pet management ability, Project Navi and abandoned pet stations. Default on. Placement needs a new game.

On: one Commerce per faction in a star system; on your colonies an alpha core lowers tariffs by 25%% instead of raising income, and improving it gives a smaller bonus. Read up on why this was needed here: bit.ly/commerce_balance. Can be turned off during an ongoing campaign to revert to vanilla behaviour (might need to re-dock). Default on.
Ships per row in most of the ship picker dialogues in the mod. Default 8.

Chance per economy tick for a meteor shower to spawn. One month has 10 ticks: 0.02 is 2%% per tick, about 18%% per month and 90%% per year. The maximum, 0.1, is about 65%% per month, so use caution. Default 0.02.
How likely a system is to have an artillery station. Lower = rarer. 1 = between 5 and 10%% of all systems will have one. Default 1. Needs a new game.
Amount of additional stations with custom types spawned on top of existing ones (0.2 = 20%% additional). Default 0.2. Needs a new game.
Automated Shipyards per Coronal Tap in the sector, rounded up. The usual 2 taps at 1.5 give 3 shipyards. Default 1.5. Needs a new game.

Master chance for a special event to be applied to an entity that does not have one. Note that the chance is actually lower as every entity has a defined chance to resolve to nothing. Default 0.9. Needs a new game.
Enables the custom station types like orbital labs and arsenal stations. Default on. Needs a new game.

defaultValue: All loot added by this mod is on top of the normal loot you would have gotten. At no point does Industrial Evolution edit, dilute, change or in any other way influence vanilla drop behaviour.

fieldDescription: Makes ship components drop from combat. Relic components still drop when this is off. Default on.

fieldName: [Commodities] Relic Component Hard Battle FP Advantage
fieldDescription: An enemy fleet drops relic components on defeat only if its FP is above your fleet's FP times this. Higher = rarer drops. Default 1.5.
Enemy FP you have to destroy for the relic component drop, as a fraction of your own fleet's FP. 0.5 = half your FP. Higher = rarer drops. Default 0.5.

defaultValue: To completely remove consumable items, go to Industrial.Evolution\data\campaign\procgen\drop_groups.csv and set the relevant group weights to 0. Deleting them will cause a crash.
All loot added by this mod is on top of the normal loot you would have gotten. At no point does Industrial Evolution edit, dilute, change or in any other way influence vanilla drop behaviour.

fieldDescription: Toggles if consumable items show up on markets. Default on.
Toggles if consumable items can drop from fleet encounters. Default on.
Toggles if the research project at Galatia Academy is available. Default on.
On: meteor showers spawn immediately instead of after a delay with an intel entry. Default off.
Minimum intensity per swarm instance. Default 1.
Maximum intensity per swarm instance. Increasing this past 4 can cause lag. Default 3.
Base width of a swarm, in game units. Default 5000.
Additional width per 1.0 intensity, in game units. Default 1000.
Upper cap for meteor count density scaling. Increasing this can cause lag. Default 2.5.
Maximum multiplier applied to runtime from intensity and conditions. Increasing this can cause lag. Default 2.5.
Baseline duration of a meteor shower in seconds. Too long = too many meteors on screen = lag. Default 50.
Cooldown in days for the same location after a swarm spawns (186 = 6 months). Default 186.
Global cooldown in days after any swarm spawns. Default 31.
Positional grid clamp for spawn calculations, in game units. Provided as setting if you use a mod that has larger than usual star systems. Default 26000.
Maximum allowed spawn distance from the system primary in game units. Default 10000.
Minimum allowed spawn distance from the system primary in game units. Default 3000.
Upper angle bound for spawn cone relative to reference axis in degrees. Default 80.
Lower angle bound for spawn cone relative to reference axis in degrees. Default 50.

defaultValue: Tip: You can disable minefields temporarily with an interdiction pulse.

fieldDescription: Time in seconds that a minefield is disabled after an interdiction pulse hits it. This is intentionally just enough time to cross once with a large fleet: minefields are intended to be an obstacle! Default 5.
Hit chance each frigate adds to its fleet's chance of getting hit by a mine. Every ship in the fleet is added up. Default 0.02.
Hit chance each destroyer adds to its fleet's chance of getting hit by a mine. Every ship in the fleet is added up. Default 0.04.
Hit chance each cruiser adds to its fleet's chance of getting hit by a mine. Every ship in the fleet is added up. Default 0.06.
Hit chance each capital ship adds to its fleet's chance of getting hit by a mine. Every ship in the fleet is added up. Default 0.12.
Mines never hit a slow fleet whose added up hit chance is below this; above it, only the part over this counts. Default 0.5.
How much a civilian ship counts toward the hit chance above. 0.5 = half. Default 0.5.
How much a phase ship counts toward the hit chance above. 0.3 = 30%%. Applies on top of the civilian mult. Default 0.3.

fieldName: [Artillery] Stars per station in a constellation
fieldDescription: At most one artillery station per this many star systems in a constellation, rounded up. Lower = more stations, more clustered; 0 = no limit. Decimals are dropped. Default 1. Needs a new game.

Time in days for watchtowers to reset to the faction controlling the artillery. This is needed to avoid "dead" artilleries after being hijacked by a pirate station and subsequently having their watchtowers taken by an invasion. Default 31.
Lower limit for the delay between shots, in seconds. If the artillery has two valid targets, it takes that long to fire at both of them. Default 2.
Upper limit for the delay between shots, in seconds. Each delay is rolled between the min and max delay. Default 3.
Lower limit for the cooldown on a single target, in seconds: it shoots at you, waits this long, then shoots again. Default 15.
Upper limit for the cooldown on a single target, in seconds. Each cooldown is rolled between the min and max cooldown. Default 17.
Multiplies the cooldown against NPC fleets, because they get demolished otherwise. Default 2.
Fleets closer to the station than this are not targeted, in units. Default 500.
Targeting range in units (12000 = 6 map cells). Improving the station adds 4000. Default 12000.
Watchtowers spot hostile fleets within this range, in units. Artillery only fires at fleets spotted by a watchtower or a hostile fleet. Default 4000.
Base FP of the fleet that spawns to defend an artillery station. Default 70.
Shells per mortar volley. They land spread around the target's predicted position. Default 8.
Seconds from a mortar volley to impact. Higher = more time to get out of the target circle. Default 5.
Explosion radius of one mortar shell, in units. Default 300.
Projectiles per railgun shot. If you increase this, also increase the fuzz mult. Default 3.
Base seconds from a railgun shot to impact. Each projectile of a shot lands one to two seconds after the one before. Higher = more time to dodge. Default 1.5.
By how much the shots miss their target. Higher = more misses. Default 0.4.
Missiles per launch. Must be even. Default 4.
Seconds from a missile launch to impact, rolled between 80%% and 120%% of this value. Default 8.
Maximum area the missiles cover; it also depends on the fuzz. Default 800.
How accurately the missiles anticipate your location. Less than 1 makes 'em kinda useless, so 1 is the minimum. Default 1.
Radius of the interdiction and slow field each missile leaves on explosion, in units. Default 200.
Seconds the slow field of a missile explosion lasts. Default 10.

Enables or disables the Commodity Forge. Default on.

Enables or disables the Interstellar Relay. Default on.

Enables or disables the Supercomputer. Default on.
Enables or disables the Embassy, also disables Ambassador management scripts. Default on.
Enables or disables the Senate. Default on.
Enables or disables the Restoration Docks. Default on. NPC placement needs a new game.
Enables or disables the Academy. Default on. NPC placement needs a new game.
Enables or disables the Requisitions Centre. Default on. NPC placement needs a new game.
Enables or disables the Engineering Hub. Default on.
Enables or disables the Courier Port. Default on. NPC placement needs a new game.
Enables or disables the Privateer Base. Default on.
Enables or disables Specialized Refining. Default on.
Enables or disables Specialized Mining. Default on.
Enables or disables the Museum. Default on.
On: planetary governments behave like vanilla Population & Infrastructure and become a cosmetic choice. Default off.

Largest colony size at which the government type can still be changed. Building up a stable colony and then changing is cheating and takes away from how these are supposed to work: higher rewards for higher difficulties. Default 3.

fieldName: [World Wonders] Cloud Painter Shield Texture Removal
fieldDescription: Makes the Cloud Painter remove the planetary shield texture so clouds stay visible. Default off.

fieldName: [World Wonders] Cloud Painter Shield Alternate Texture
fieldDescription: Replaces the planetary shield texture with a colourless alternative, so clouds stay visible and the shield is still perceptible. Does nothing while Cloud Painter Shield Texture Removal is on. Default off.
On: Variable industry output goes to the gathering point instead of local storage. Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
Core run time in days until burn out. Tooltips will be broken if number is not a multiple of 31. Default 558.
Core run time in days until burn out. Tooltips will be broken if number is not a multiple of 31. Default 279.
Core run time in days until burn out. Tooltips will be broken if number is not a multiple of 31. Default 93.
Required Relic Components per FP for zero D-Mods. Default 2.
Base D-Mod count on ships built via the Yards. Default 5.
How much ship components count toward the Salvage Yards budget, as a multiple of their standard cost. 1.2 = every component counts 1.2 times its cost. Default 1.2.
Days until a Salvage Yards ship order is delivered. Applies to new orders. Default 60. Italian Sounds while person on crotch rocket delivers Paragon to hungry space captain.

fieldName: [Salvage Yards] D-Mod Moving Base Cost Mult
fieldDescription: Cost to move one D-Mod, as a multiple of what restoring that D-Mod costs. 0.8 = moving is 20%% cheaper than restoring. Relations still change the final price. Default 0.8.

Disable the auto-whitelist and return to the strict manual entry based whitelist system. This means that only ships that are listed in the reverse_engineering.csv whitelist are eligible to be researched. Default off.

On: the Engineering Hub accepts ships without the whitelist checks. Yes, this is the one you are looking for (NOTE: post version 4.0 has an auto-whitelist that is much broader and you may not need this setting anymore). Default off.

fieldName: [Engineering Hub] Auto Transfer BP to Gathering Point
fieldDescription: On: the Engineering Hub delivers finished ship blueprints to the gathering point instead of local storage. Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
Extra credits per D-Mod removed from a frigate at Restoration Docks on markets you do not own. Default 1000.
Extra credits per D-Mod removed from a destroyer at Restoration Docks on markets you do not own. Default 3000.
Extra credits per D-Mod removed from a cruiser at Restoration Docks on markets you do not own. Default 7000.
Extra credits per D-Mod removed from a capital ship at Restoration Docks on markets you do not own. Default 10000.
Cost and time multiplier for restoring Ruined Infrastructure. 0.5 = half the normal cost and time. Running restorations keep their time. Default 0.5.
All derelict industry output will be delivered to the gathering point instead of local storage. Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
Days the Rift Generator needs to recharge after moving a planet. An alpha core cuts 30 days. Default 90.
Range in light years for the target system of a planet move. A beta core adds 3. Default 9.
Auto-deliver restored forge templates to the closest HullDecon. Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
On: the Hull Deconstructor takes any ship except printed ones and ships with a permanent non AI officer. Leave this one alone, you want the engineering hub. Default on.

fieldName: [Hull Deconstructor] Allow Deconstructing the Nex Omega Merc
fieldDescription: On: the Hull Deconstructor accepts Nexerelin mercenary ships, which lets you dupe the Omega ship. Added on request :) Default off.
Auto-deliver finished forge templates to the closest HullForge. Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
Days to deconstruct a frigate into a forge template. Default 10.
Days to deconstruct a destroyer into a forge template. Default 20.
Days to deconstruct a cruiser into a forge template. Default 30.
Days to deconstruct a capital ship into a forge template. Default 40.
On: the Hull Forge prints ships off a template until it is empty. Off: the template goes to storage after one run. Default on.
Auto-deliver degraded forge templates to the closest lab, or empty ones to a Deconstructor (AI core effect only). Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
Days to print a frigate from a forge template. Default 5.
Days to print a destroyer from a forge template. Default 10.
Days to print a cruiser from a forge template. Default 15.
Days to print a capital ship from a forge template. Default 20.
Chance per day that a hireable officer shows up at a colony with an Academy, if it has none. 0.15 = 15%%. Default 0.15.
Chance per day that a hireable administrator shows up at a colony with an Academy, if it has none. 0.10 = 10%%. Default 0.1.
Days to move an officer's personality one step. AI cores shorten it. Default 93.
Credits paid when an officer starts personality training. Default 30000.
Days to teach an administrator a new skill. AI cores shorten it. Default 124.
Credits paid when an administrator starts training. Default 20000.
Credits per month for each officer or administrator stored at an Academy you do not own. Default 2000.
The maximum credits a ship can earn per month while exhibited. Default 1950.
The minimum credits a ship can earn per month while exhibited. If the maximum is lower, it is raised to this value. Default 50.
Parade slots without modifiers. Default 1.
Maximum number of ships allowed to participate in a single parade. Parades already out keep their ships. Default 15.
Minimum number of ships required to initiate a parade. Default 3.

fieldName: [Museum] Top Ship Pool Amount for Parade Selection
fieldDescription: Number of ships considered during random parade participant selection, counting down from the highest valued one. Default 20.
Immigration bonus granted while a parade fleet is active. Default 5.
Stability bonus granted while a parade fleet is active. Default 1.
Additional parade capacity gained when the structure is improved. Default 1.
Extra parade slots provided when an Alpha Core is installed. Default 1.
Amount of required income per +1 stability when a Beta Core is installed. Default 20000.

fieldName: [Museum] Beta Core Income per Point Immigration
fieldDescription: Amount of required income per +1 immigration when a Beta Core is installed. Default 3000.
Multiplier applied to total income when a Gamma Core is installed. Default 1.3.
Multiplier applied to the value of rare / non-learnable ships. Default 2.

fieldName: [Courier Port] Base Cost per cargo unit
fieldDescription: Transport cost per cargo space used. Some items take more space than others: a nanoforge takes 10 cargo space. Affected by distance. Applies to new shipments. Default 5.

fieldName: [Courier Port] Base Cost per ship unit
fieldDescription: Transport cost per ship DP. Larger ship, larger cost. Affected by distance. Applies to new shipments. Default 170.
The base fee of a shipment, not affected by distance. Applies to new shipments. Default 1000.
This setting changes how impactful distance is to the cost calculation. The higher the value, the more distance will factor in. Applies to new shipments. Default 1.

fieldName: [Privateer Base] Raid only for Unknown BPs
fieldDescription: On: the Privateer Base only raids blueprints you do not know. Off: a mix of known and unknown ones. Default off.
Auto-deliver the looted items to the gathering point. Remember, the Courier Port exists. Default off.
